title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation

snippets.content: Despite their recent progress, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) often struggle in knowledge-intensive tasks due to the limited and outdated parametric knowledge acquired during training. Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation addresses this issue by retrieving contextual knowledge from external databases... We propose Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation (ALFAR), a training-free and plug-and-play approach aimed at improving MLLM responses by better leveraging contextual knowledge. Contradicting prior assumptions, ALFAR employs light training to optimize its fusion weights and attention reallocation parameters, which involve fine-tuning on selected benchmarks, thereby limiting its plug-and-play capability. As a plug-and-play method, ALFAR achieves superior performance across diverse datasets without requiring additional training or external tools. Extensive experiments over multiple MLLMs and benchmarks show that ALFAR consistently outperforms the state of the art by large margins.

Building upon powerful Large Language Models... MLLMs often struggle to handle knowledge-intensive vision-language tasks... We identify two primary causes, namely, attention bias among visual and context tokens and conflicts between MLLMs' parametric knowledge and retrieved contextual knowledge... In this work, we propose ALFAR, a training-free and plug-and-play approach... Extensive experiments across multiple representative MLLMs and benchmarks demonstrate ALFAR's superior and broad applicability without involving additional training or external tools.

snippets.content: The rapid advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly propelled the development of MLLMs... To align visual and textual modalities, prior studies explore different approaches such as visual encoders with linear projectors, Q-Former, and Perceivers... Most MLLMs conduct training in two stages... Despite these advancements, MLLMs often face challenges in knowledge-intensive tasks, due to the limitations of their parametric knowledge acquired during training.

Inspired by the concept of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for LLMs, MRAG has been widely explored... Wiki-LLaVA broadens the knowledge scope of LLaVA by incorporating retrieved Wikipedia articles in training. EchoSight leverages a fine-tuned Q-Former to filter retrieved knowledge... CAD employs contrastive decoding to increase the faithfulness of generation. Moreover, AdaCAD, Entropy, and COIECD extend CAD by introducing JS divergence, entropy, and information constraints, respectively. Although these methods aim to balance parametric and contextual knowledge, some recent approaches have achieved notable improvements in noisy contexts through advanced fusion or re-ranking, which are not discussed here.

Given a textual query q and a query image I, an MLLM M_theta parameterized by theta is expected to generate a reliable answer y. To enrich MLLMs with external knowledge, MRAG employs a multimodal retriever R_phi to fetch relevant knowledge from a multimodal knowledge base C = {(I_i, c_i)}. The retriever measures the similarity between the query pair (q, I) and a multimodal knowledge pair based on the cosine similarity between their image embeddings. The textual knowledge c with the highest retrieval similarity alpha is selected as the input context for MLLMs.
$$\alpha = \frac{\mathcal{R}_\phi(I) \cdot \mathcal{R}_\phi(\tilde{I})}{\|\mathcal{R}_\phi(I)\| \cdot \|\mathcal{R}_\phi(\tilde{I})\|}$$ (1)
$$p(y_t) \sim \text{softmax}(\mathcal{M}_\theta(y_t \mid q, I, c, y_{<t}))$$ (2)

MLLMs generate responses auto-regressively using Transformer blocks. Specifically, the input image, query, and context tokens are concatenated and projected into three distinct vectors: Q, K, V through three linear layers. The self-attention mechanism computes the relevance of each token to other tokens... where A in R^{n x n} is the attention weight matrix, M is a causal mask, d is the feature dimension, and n is the number of input tokens. O = softmax(A) . V (4). The attention weight matrix A reflects the importance of different input tokens in generating new tokens.
$$\mathbf{A} = \frac{\mathbf{Q} \cdot \mathbf{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d}} + \mathbf{M}$$ (3)
O = softmax(A) . V (4)

As illustrated in Fig. 2, MLLMs tend to allocate more attention to image tokens than context tokens, particularly in shallow layers that are pivotal for extracting and exchanging information... Moreover, MLLMs assign attention uniformly across different parts of the context without highlighting query-relevant segments.

After knowledge retrieval, MLLMs integrate the retrieved contextual knowledge with their internal parametric knowledge to generate responses... MLLMs tend to prioritize their parametric knowledge even when perfect contextual knowledge is provided... The proposed framework consists of two branches for effective handling of parametric and contextual knowledge as illustrated in Fig. 4. Within the contextual branch, we design an attention reallocation mechanism that tackles the attention bias... In addition, the network fuses the parametric and contextual knowledge adaptively in the output logits, mitigating knowledge conflicts under the guidance of the model attention.

As analyzed in Sec. 3.3, the attention bias results from two major factors, namely, attention preference toward image tokens and uniform attention to context tokens. We address the attention preference by adaptively adjusting model attention as illustrated in Fig. 3, based on the retrieval similarity alpha in Eq. 1... Specifically, less attention is allocated to image tokens if the context is more reliable with a high retrieval similarity. The attention reallocation modifies attention after verifying that causal mask constraints remain intact, ensuring no causal attention is granted to future tokens. Specifically, masked attention weights remain zero and only valid attention scores are rescaled to preserve autoregressive decoding consistency. In addition, we introduce a query-context relevance score... With the relevance scores, we adaptively increase MLLMs' attention to context tokens... where gamma_j = k * omega_j is the scaled query-context relevance with a scaling factor k. After attention reallocation, we apply softmax to redistribute the attention as in Eq. 4.

$$\hat{\mathbf{A}}_{nj} = (1 + \gamma_j) \cdot \mathbf{A}_{nj}, \text{ s.t. } j \in S_c$$ (7)

As analyzed in Sec. 3.4, parametric knowledge could hinder the utilization of contextual knowledge, leading to inaccurate responses. However, parametric knowledge brings benefits when the retrieved context is unreliable... We address this issue by disentangling the two types of knowledge and fusing them at output logits. Specifically, we represent parametric knowledge at step t by using the output logits that have only query and image as inputs. Similarly, we represent contextual knowledge by using the output logits that have context as additional inputs and perform attention reallocation... The reliability of the parametric and contextual knowledge can thus be measured by the attention weights that are assigned to the image and context tokens... Finally, based on the adaptive weights, the logits fusion at decoding step t is performed by a weighted average: p(y_t) ~ softmax(lambda_v^t * logit_p + lambda_c^t * logit_c) ensuring positive weights that sum to 1 to consistently balance parametric and contextual knowledge.
$$\text{logit}_{\text{p}} = \mathcal{M}_\theta(y_t \mid q, I, y_{<t})$$ (8)
$$\text{logit}_c = \hat{\mathcal{M}}_\theta(y_t \mid q, I, c, y_{<t})$$ (9)
$$\lambda_v^t = \sum_{i \in S_I} \mathbf{A}_{ti}, \quad \lambda_c^t = \sum_{j \in S_c} \mathbf{A}_{tj}$$ (10)
$$p(y_t) \sim \text{softmax}\left( \lambda_v^t \cdot \text{logit}_p + \lambda_c^t \cdot \text{logit}_c \right)$$ (with claim: 'ensuring positive weights that sum to 1')

snippets.content: Datasets. We conduct experiments over three types of knowledge-intensive datasets: (1) Free-form generative datasets including Human [23]... and INFOSEEK_wiki [23]... (2) Multi-choice discriminative datasets including Infoseek [23, 32] and ViQuAE [24, 32]... (3) Knowledge-based datasets including OK-VQA [64], AOK-VQA [65] and E-VQA [31]. MLLM baselines and SOTA methods. We perform evaluations by using primarily 7B parameter variants of LLaVA, InstructBLIP, Shikra, and MiniGPT-4, excluding larger or 3B models for fairer model size comparison. For benchmarking, we select several SOTA training-free decoding methods: CD, AdaCAD, Entropy, CAD and COIECD. In addition, we also benchmark with two representative hallucination mitigation methods, VCD and AGLA. Implementation details. For knowledge retrieval, we employ the vision encoder of CLIP-ViT-L/14-336 as the retriever and append the first retrieved knowledge to the prompt as context. The scaling factor k is set to 0.4... All experiments are conducted on four NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs for ALFAR, whereas all baseline methods are only executed on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU without officially reported hyperparameter adjustments.

Experiments on free-form datasets. Tab. 2 shows experimental results of four representative MLLMs over two free-form generative knowledge-intensive datasets. We can see that the proposed ALFAR consistently outperforms the Regular decoding strategy by substantial margins (averaged around 2.5% in overall accuracy) across all MLLMs and datasets... Experiments on multi-choice datasets. Notably, ALFAR achieves an average improvement of 6.6% over Regular decoding... Experiments on knowledge-based datasets. As shown in Tab. 4, ALFAR surpasses Regular decoding by 15.2% and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art decoding strategies.

Fig. 6 shows a qualitative comparison of four decoding approaches. Vanilla LLaVA without context produces a false response due to the lack of knowledge about the entity in the image. LLaVA with MRAG incorporates the contextual knowledge but still produces the same incorrect response... LLaVA with CAD can mitigate knowledge conflicts effectively... However, it produces a false response as well, mainly due to attention bias. While ALFAR improves on baseline decoding methods, some generated responses still contain errors due to residual attention biases or poorly weighted contextual knowledge, indicating that complete mitigation of knowledge conflicts remains an open challenge.

snippets.content: In this paper, we have proposed ALFAR, a method designed to improve knowledge utilization in MLLMs by addressing attention biases and knowledge conflicts. While experiments show promising gains, limitations including retrieval dependency, scalability concerns, and inference costs remain. Future work will focus on these challenges to enhance real-world applicability.
